prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one ORIGINAL MASTER painting for one Bhagavad Gita verse in a Sanskrit reader. Generate a single square 1:1 image, 2048x2048 or the highest actually supported native square resolution. Consistent series style: refined traditional Indian watercolor and restrained gouache on warm ivory handmade paper; fine organic detail, subtle ochre, sage, dusty terracotta and muted indigo; dignified ancient Indian setting, quiet atmospheric daylight. The image must illustrate THIS VERSE'S ACTUAL MEANING. Read the exact source meaning below; derive a concrete, intelligible scene or a restrained symbolic interpretation of that teaching. Never simply paint an unrelated chariot, generic temple or anonymous landscape. Compose one coherent scene, no collage or infographic. Keep important faces, hands, relationships and narrative objects inside the central 60% of width and central 50% of height, surrounded by ample low-detail sky, ground and paper atmosphere. No important subject cut by an edge. This one master must support portrait/landscape phones and tablets through safe proportional fitting. No text of any kind, no verse number, no letters, no Sanskrit/Roman typography, no watermark, no frame, no UI. Text will be rendered separately by the app over the image at a user-adjustable default image opacity of 48%. If Krishna is depicted, maintain a youthful calm blue-skinned figure in muted golden-yellow garments, a restrained peacock-feather crown, no modern jewelry. Arjuna is a dark-haired warrior with a small crown, bow and understated bronze armor. Use them only when the meaning warrants them; the scene or analogy remains verse-specific.  Reference (DO NOT DRAW THIS TEXT): Bhagavad Gītā 11.36. Exact Sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच ।
स्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्या
जगत्प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च ।
रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्ति
सर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसंघाः ॥ ३६ ॥ Exact stored meaning: Arjuna said: O Hṛṣīkeśa (master of the senses), it is right and fitting that the world is delighted and becomes deeply enamored at the singing of Your glory. The rākṣasas, terror-stricken, flee in all directions, while all the assemblies of siddhas (perfected beings) bow to You. Chapter context: The universal vision granted to Arjuna. Follow the verse-specific appearance, emotional response or prayer. Awe and cosmic scale, but no gore or graphic violence; when cosmic destruction is stated, use symbolic silhouettes and radiance. Previous verse context only, do not substitute for the target: Sañjaya said: Having heard this utterance of Keśava, the crowned one (Kirīṭī, Arjuna) — trembling, hands folded in reverence — bowed to Kṛṣṇa, and once more prostrating himself in great fear, spoke with a voice choked with emotion — Next verse context only, do not substitute for the target: O great soul (Mahātman), why should they not bow to You — who are greater even than Brahmā, the original creator? O Infinite (Ananta)! O Lord of the gods (Deveśa)! O Abode of the universe (Jagannivāsa)! You are that imperishable (Akṣara) which is beyond both sat (being) and asat (non-being) — that supreme Reality. Final instruction: center the distinctive content of the TARGET meaning, not the neighboring verses. No fabricated teaching or unrelated religious scene.
review_note: Contact-sheet inspection; conservative full-frame safe region preserves all figures and objects.

The rākṣasas, terror-stricken, flee in all directions, while all the assemblies of siddhas (perfected beings) bow to You.
